label: copy-phase echo of z/x/s/0/f/g/e/w/t/r in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never during the original tokens or on the <DEL> step, and never at recall_idx 0. It is much more likely to fire in long sequences: L=9 carries 65% of the activation mass and L<=5 almost none. Its rate peaks at recall_idx 2 (a bit before the middle of the copy) and again on the last outputs of L=8/9 sequences (t=16,17). The fed-back input token matters a lot: z (4.4x lift), x, s, 0, f, g, e, w, t and r have the highest rates. Copy phase plus L>=8 plus that token set gives dev F1 0.53 and mass recall 0.72. Precision stays below 0.5, and the position and token effects interact in ways no simple predicate captured, so this is a partial description. Magnitude is small (max 0.017), and the largest activations are mostly on z inputs late in L=9 copies. It does not fire on the first copy step, the original phase, or short sequences.
